title: Proof\
body_md:
For $M>0$ and $\gamma>0$, Markov's inequality gives
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\bigg\{\sum_{t=1}^T\mu_t\epsilon_t\ge M\bigg\}&=\mathbb{P}\bigg\{\exp\bigg(\gamma\sum_{t=1}^T\mu_t\epsilon_t\bigg)\ge\exp(\gamma M)\bigg\}\\
&\le\exp(-\gamma M)\mathbb{E}\exp\bigg(\gamma\sum_{t=1}^T\mu_t\epsilon_t\bigg)\\
&=\exp(-\gamma M)\mathbb{E}\bigg\{\mathbb{E}\bigg[\exp\bigg(\gamma\sum_{t=1}^T\mu_t\epsilon_t\bigg)\bigg|\mathcal{G}_T\bigg]\bigg\}\\
&\le\exp(-\gamma M)\mathbb{E}\exp\bigg(\gamma\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\mu_t\epsilon_t+\frac{\gamma^2\mu_T^2}8\bigg)\\
&\le\exp(-\gamma M)\mathbb{E}\exp\bigg(\gamma\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\mu_t\epsilon_t+\frac{\gamma^2C^2}8\bigg)\\
&\le\exp(-\gamma M+\gamma^2C^2T/8).
\end{align*}
where the second inequality holds by the conditional moment bound given $\mathcal{G}_T$, the third inequality holds because $|\mu_t|\le C$ almost surely, and the last inequality holds by recursively applying the inequalities. Taking $\gamma=4M/(C^2T)$ gives
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}\bigg\{\sum_{t=1}^T\mu_t\epsilon_t\ge M\bigg\}\le\exp\Big(-\frac{2M^2}{C^2T}\Big).
\end{align*}
For $M=0$, the asserted bound is $1$.
